name: Enoxaparin
executiveSummary: LMWH. Adult prophylaxis: **40 mg SC/day** (surgical **20–40 mg** by risk). Treatment DVT/PE/ACS: **1 mg/kg SC q12h** or **1.5 mg/kg/day**. If CrCl <30: often **1 mg/kg/day**. Pediatrics: **0.5–1 mg/kg** by indication.
indications:
## Indications

- Prophylaxis and treatment of DVT/PE; ACS (with antiplatelets); anticoagulation bridge; pregnancy (preferred vs VKA).

## Precautions

- Bleeding; HIT (less than UFH).
- Not IM. Avoid with recent spinal/epidural anesthesia without protocol.
- Anti-Xa in pregnancy, weight extremes, CKD.

> Prefilled syringes 20–40–60–80–100 mg; do not expel air bubble (by design).

adulto.dose: Medical prophylaxis: **40 mg SC/day**. High-risk surgery: **40 mg/day** (start 12 h before/after per protocol). Treatment: **1 mg/kg q12h** or **1.5 mg/kg/day**. ACS: **1 mg/kg q12h**. CrCl <30: **1 mg/kg/day** treatment; prophylaxis **20–30 mg/day**.
adulto.administration: SC abdomen (rotate sites); do not rub.
adulto.notes: Use actual body weight for mg/kg; obesity: anti-Xa/protocol.

pediatrico.dose: Prophylaxis: ~**0.5 mg/kg q12h**. Treatment: **1 mg/kg q12h** (neonates often **1.5–1.7 mg/kg q12h**) — hematology + anti-Xa.
pediatrico.notes: Do not extrapolate adult without weight.

neonatal.dose: Treatment often **1.5–1.7 mg/kg SC q12h** — protocol + anti-Xa only.

stability:
## Stability

- Room temp per label; do not freeze.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Injection-site hematoma, bleeding, anemia; rare: HIT, hyperkalemia, skin necrosis.
